title: High-confidence shortcut hallucinations that evade concept-vector detectors

original_idea.body: Test whether concept-vector hallucination probes miss high-confidence shortcut hallucinations. Inference-only, open model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a structural blind spot in probe-based monitoring for the most dangerous hallucinations directly bears on monitor reliability (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Curate shortcut prompts + run probe; clear methodology, prompt curation needs care (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (blind-spot rate vs ordinary hallucinations), prompt-set construction adds modest effort (level 4).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly monitor-evaluation work on open models, neglected by labs (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only on small curated prompt set, near free-tier (level 5).

novelty.reasoning: High-certainty hallucination evasion noted; testing concept-vector detectors specifically may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Phenomenon documented for detectors generally; concept-vector-probe test may be open.
